title: Goodwill: Nature and Valuation
summary: Goodwill is the value of a firm's reputation that enables it to earn more than a normal return on its capital. This chapter explains the nature of goodwill, the factors that affect it, why partnership firms need to value it, and the average profit, super profit and capitalisation methods of valuation.

notes.heading: Meaning and nature of goodwill
notes.html:
Goodwill is the monetary value of the reputation and business connections of a firm which help it earn profits above the normal level earned by similar firms. It is the present value of expected future super profits.

  • It is an intangible asset (it has no physical existence but has value); it is not a fictitious asset.
  • It cannot be sold separately; it is realised only when the whole business (or a share in it) is sold.
  • Its value can change quickly with changes in management, competition and market conditions.
  • Under AS-26 (Intangible Assets), only purchased goodwill (paid for in money or money's worth) is recorded in the books. Self-generated (inherent) goodwill is not recorded.

notes.heading: Factors affecting the value of goodwill
notes.html:
• Nature of business: a firm dealing in products with stable demand earns steadier profits and has higher goodwill.
  • Location: a business located at a busy, convenient place attracts more customers.
  • Efficiency of management: good management raises productivity and profits.
  • Market situation: monopoly or limited competition increases goodwill.
  • Special advantages: import licences, patents, trademarks, long-term contracts, cheap power supply.
  • Quality of products and customer relations: loyal customers ensure repeat sales.
  • Period of existence: an older, established firm usually has a larger customer base.

notes.heading: Need for valuing goodwill in a partnership
notes.html:
Goodwill belongs to all partners in their profit-sharing ratio. Whenever a partner gains or sacrifices a share of future profits, the goodwill must be valued so that the gaining partner compensates the sacrificing partner. Valuation is needed on:

  1. Change in the profit-sharing ratio among existing partners
  2. Admission of a new partner
  3. Retirement of a partner
  4. Death of a partner
  5. Dissolution of the firm when the business is sold as a going concern
  6. Amalgamation of two partnership firms

notes.heading: Average profit method (simple average)
notes.html:
Goodwill = Average profit x Number of years' purchase. The number of years' purchase is the number of years for which the firm is expected to keep earning such profits because of its reputation.

Normalise past profits before averaging:

  • Deduct abnormal gains (e.g. profit on sale of a fixed asset, an insurance claim surplus, income from non-trade investments).
  • Add back abnormal losses (e.g. loss by fire or theft, loss on sale of a fixed asset).
  • Deduct a fair remuneration for partners if it was not charged.
  • A loss of any year is subtracted while totalling.

Worked illustration 1

Profits: 2021-22 ₹1,20,000; 2022-23 ₹1,50,000 (including a gain of ₹10,000 on sale of furniture); 2023-24 ₹1,10,000 (after an abnormal loss of ₹20,000 by fire); 2024-25 ₹1,60,000. Goodwill is to be valued at 2 years' purchase of average profits.

YearProfit ₹Adjustment ₹Normal profit ₹
2021-221,20,000—1,20,000
2022-231,50,000(10,000)1,40,000
2023-241,10,000+20,0001,30,000
2024-251,60,000—1,60,000
Total5,50,000

Average profit = 5,50,000 / 4 = ₹1,37,500. Goodwill = 1,37,500 x 2 = ₹2,75,000.

notes.heading: Weighted average profit method
notes.html:
Used when profits show a rising or falling trend, so that recent years get more importance. Weights are usually 1, 2, 3 ... with the latest year getting the highest weight.

Weighted average profit = Sum of (Profit x Weight) / Sum of weights.

Worked illustration 2

Profits: 2022-23 ₹90,000; 2023-24 ₹1,20,000; 2024-25 ₹1,50,000. Weights 1, 2, 3. Goodwill at 3 years' purchase.

YearProfit ₹WeightProduct ₹
2022-2390,000190,000
2023-241,20,00022,40,000
2024-251,50,00034,50,000
Total67,80,000

Weighted average profit = 7,80,000 / 6 = ₹1,30,000. Goodwill = 1,30,000 x 3 = ₹3,90,000.

notes.heading: Super profit method
notes.html:
Super profit = Average (actual) profit − Normal profit, where Normal profit = Capital employed x Normal rate of return / 100.

Capital employed = Total assets (excluding goodwill, fictitious assets such as debit balance of P&L, and non-trade investments) − Outside liabilities. Alternatively: Partners' capitals + Reserves and accumulated profits − Goodwill − Fictitious assets − Non-trade investments.

Goodwill = Super profit x Number of years' purchase.

Worked illustration 3

Assets of a firm: Land ₹6,00,000; Machinery ₹4,00,000; Stock ₹2,50,000; Debtors ₹2,00,000; Cash ₹50,000; Goodwill (in books) ₹50,000. Liabilities: Creditors ₹3,00,000; Bank loan ₹2,00,000. Average profit ₹1,60,000; normal rate of return 10%. Goodwill at 3 years' purchase of super profit.

notes.heading: Capitalisation method
notes.html:
(a) Capitalisation of average profit

  1. Capitalised value of average profit = Average profit x 100 / Normal rate of return. This is the capital that 'should' be needed to earn the average profit at the normal rate.
  2. Goodwill = Capitalised value − Actual capital employed.

(b) Capitalisation of super profit

Goodwill = Super profit x 100 / Normal rate of return.

Using the data of illustration 3: (a) Capitalised value = 1,60,000 x 100/10 = ₹16,00,000; Goodwill = 16,00,000 − 10,00,000 = ₹6,00,000. (b) Goodwill = 60,000 x 100/10 = ₹6,00,000. Both methods always give the same answer for the same data, which is a useful check.

If the capitalised value is less than capital employed, there is no goodwill (negative goodwill is not recorded in partnership questions).

notes.heading: Hidden goodwill and common mistakes
notes.html:
Hidden goodwill arises when goodwill is not given but is implied by the capital brought in by a new partner. It is worked out in the admission chapter: Goodwill = Total capital of new firm implied by the new partner's contribution − Actual total capital (after adjustments) of all partners.

Common mistakes

  • Taking capital employed including goodwill or non-trade investments.
  • Forgetting to deduct income from non-trade investments from average profit when those investments are excluded from capital employed.
  • Not deducting partners' fair remuneration from profits.
  • Adding a loss year as a positive figure.
  • Multiplying average profit (not super profit) by years' purchase under the super profit method.

options: Fictitious asset
Intangible asset
Current asset
Tangible wasting asset
mcqs.explanation: Goodwill has no physical form but has value, so it is an intangible asset; it is not fictitious because it can fetch a price when the business is sold.

mcqs.q: Capital employed is ₹5,00,000, normal rate of return 12% and average profit ₹80,000. Goodwill at 3 years' purchase of super profit is:
Super profit is ₹24,000 and the normal rate of return is 12%. Goodwill by capitalisation of super profit is:
Profits of the last three years were ₹60,000, ₹(15,000) loss and ₹75,000. Goodwill at 3 years' purchase of average profit is:

Assertion (A): Self-generated goodwill is not recorded in the books of a partnership firm.
Reason (R): As per AS-26, only goodwill acquired for consideration is recognised as an asset.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
mcqs.explanation: AS-26 does not allow recognition of internally generated goodwill because its cost cannot be measured reliably; this explains A.

mcqs.q: Which of the following does NOT affect the value of goodwill of a firm?
options: Location of the business
Efficiency of management
Drawings made by partners
Nature of the business
mcqs.explanation: Drawings are personal withdrawals and have no effect on the firm's ability to earn super profits.

mcqs.q: Total assets of a firm are ₹8,00,000, including goodwill of ₹50,000. Outside liabilities are ₹1,50,000. Capital employed is:
Profits for three years were ₹30,000, ₹45,000 and ₹60,000 with weights 1, 2 and 3 respectively. Goodwill at 2 years' purchase of weighted average profit is:

Case: The average profit of a firm is ₹1,00,000. The partners have not charged any remuneration, though a fair remuneration for their services would be ₹20,000 p.a. Goodwill is to be valued at 2 years' purchase of average profit. Goodwill is:

Assertion (A): While computing average profit, an abnormal loss suffered in an earlier year is added back to that year's profit.
Reason (R): Abnormal items are recurring in nature.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
mcqs.explanation: A is true. R is false: abnormal items are non-recurring, which is exactly why they are removed when estimating future maintainable profit.

mcqs.q: Average profit ₹90,000; normal rate of return 15%; capital employed ₹5,00,000. Goodwill by capitalisation of average profit is:
Under the super profit method, goodwill is equal to:
options: Average profit x Number of years' purchase
Super profit x Number of years' purchase
Normal profit x Number of years' purchase
Capital employed x Normal rate of return
mcqs.explanation: Only the excess (super) profit is attributed to goodwill, multiplied by the expected number of years.

questions.answerHtml: Goodwill is the value of the reputation of a firm, in terms of money, that enables it to earn profits higher than the normal profits earned by similar firms.

questions.q: Name any two methods of valuing goodwill.
questions.answerHtml:
• Average profit method
  • Super profit method (also: capitalisation method)

questions.q: Explain any three factors that affect the value of goodwill of a firm.
questions.answerHtml:
1. Nature of business: a firm making products with steady demand earns stable profits and has more goodwill.
  2. Location: a centrally located business with easy customer access earns more and has higher goodwill.
  3. Efficiency of management: competent management improves productivity and reduces cost, raising profits and goodwill.

questions.q: Profits of a firm were: 2021-22 ₹90,000; 2022-23 ₹1,00,000 (including a profit of ₹15,000 on sale of machinery); 2023-24 ₹65,000 (after an abnormal loss of ₹30,000 due to flood). Calculate goodwill at 2 years' purchase of average profit.

A firm's total assets are ₹9,00,000, which include goodwill of ₹50,000 and non-trade investments of ₹50,000. Outside liabilities are ₹2,00,000. Average profit is ₹1,10,000, which includes income from non-trade investments of ₹5,000. Normal rate of return is 15%. Calculate goodwill at 4 years' purchase of super profit.
questions.answerHtml:
1. Capital employed = 9,00,000 − 50,000 (goodwill) − 50,000 (non-trade investments) − 2,00,000 = ₹6,00,000
  2. Adjusted average profit = 1,10,000 − 5,000 = ₹1,05,000
  3. Normal profit = 6,00,000 x 15/100 = ₹90,000
  4. Super profit = 1,05,000 − 90,000 = ₹15,000
  5. Goodwill = 15,000 x 4 = ₹60,000

questions.q: Calculate goodwill at 3 years' purchase of weighted average profit. Profits: 2022-23 ₹1,02,000 (weight 1); 2023-24 ₹1,20,000 (weight 2); 2024-25 ₹1,50,000 (weight 3). The profit of 2024-25 includes an abnormal gain of ₹10,000.

A firm has assets of ₹20,00,000 (excluding goodwill) and outside liabilities of ₹5,00,000. Its average profit is ₹2,10,000 and the normal rate of return is 12%. Calculate goodwill by (a) capitalisation of average profit, (b) capitalisation of super profit and (c) 3 years' purchase of super profit.
questions.answerHtml:
Working: Capital employed = 20,00,000 − 5,00,000 = ₹15,00,000. Normal profit = 15,00,000 x 12% = ₹1,80,000. Super profit = 2,10,000 − 1,80,000 = ₹30,000.

  1. Capitalisation of average profit: Capitalised value = 2,10,000 x 100/12 = ₹17,50,000. Goodwill = 17,50,000 − 15,00,000 = ₹2,50,000.
  2. Capitalisation of super profit: 30,000 x 100/12 = ₹2,50,000 (same as (a), confirming the working).
  3. Super profit method: 30,000 x 3 = ₹90,000.

questions.q: Profits of a firm for four years were ₹1,50,000, ₹1,80,000, ₹1,60,000 and ₹2,10,000. Partners did not charge any remuneration; a fair remuneration would be ₹30,000 p.a. The firm's capital employed is ₹10,00,000 and the normal rate of return is 10%. Calculate goodwill (a) at 2.5 years' purchase of average profit and (b) at 3 years' purchase of super profit.
